primary_secondary.note: Both describe the authors' own commit mining, survey and 13 interviews at NAV IT.

gl_type.claude: Article (arXiv pre-print of a research paper)

dora_applied.note: Neither reports DORA in the source.

space_applied.note: SPACE cited in the Discussion for its emphasis on satisfaction, flow and collaboration; not the measurement instrument.

ai_discussed.note: GitHub Copilot adoption is the object of study.

remote_covid.note: Neither mentions remote work or COVID-19.

data_window.claude: Commits over 105 weeks (two years, no dates); interviews November–December 2023; survey March–April 2024
data_window.note: Both give only a two-year (105-week) commit window without dates; interview and survey dates come from Claude only.

cat_productivity.note: Productivity is only perceived (survey item); task-speed figures are cited from other studies.

cat_quality.note: Structural code quality metrics (function complexity, average module size).

cat_collaboration.note: Collaboration only via the SPACE remark in the Discussion.

cat_satisfaction.note: Thin basis: interview findings on enjoyment/fun and reduced frustration; recommendation framed as investment in developer satisfaction and retention.

cat_activity.note: Weekly commits, lines added/deleted, net lines changed (six commit-based activity metrics).

cat_devex.note: Flow and cognitive load discussed, but not the DevEx framework.

cat_agile.note: Agile organization is context only; no process metrics.

cat_survey.note: Perceived productivity change on a 5-point scale (-2 to +2); interviews.

evidence.quote: This study investigates the real-world impact of the generative AI (GenAI) tool GitHub Copilot on developer activity and perceived productivity.
We analyzed 26,317 unique non-merge commits from 703 of NAV IT's GitHub repositories over a two-year period, focusing on commit-based activity metrics from 25 Copilot users and 14 non-users.
